\chapter{How's It Going?}
\label{ch:hi-hows-it-going}
\hlchaptermodality{123}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can greet someone the everyday way: how's it going, all well, long time, what's up, have you eaten.}

Complete HI-C123-khana-khaya: everyday greetings.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[kyā hāl hai?]{\hi{क्या} \hi{हाल} \hi{है}? (kyā hāl hai?) — how's it going?}

\label{lesson:HI-C123-kyahaal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for permission to go, then the Hindi for I have to go.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{क्या} \hi{हाल} \hi{है}?}
\textbf{\hi{क्या} \hi{हाल} \hi{है}?} (\emph{kyā hāl hai?}) — \textquotedblleft{}how's it going?\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}how are things?\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{हाल}} is \textquotedblleft{}condition, state\textquotedblright{}. Friendlier than \textbf{\hi{आप} \hi{कैसे} \hi{हैं}?}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An everyday opener.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kyā hāl hai?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kyā hāl hai?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{kyā hāl hai?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for permission to go, then the Hindi for I have to go, then say \emph{kyā hāl hai?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{क्या} \hi{हाल} \hi{है}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}How's it going?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sab ṭhīk?]{\hi{सब} \hi{ठीक}? (sab ṭhīk?) — all well?}

\label{lesson:HI-C123-sabthik}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for I have to go, then the Hindi for how's it going.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सब} \hi{ठीक}?}
\textbf{\hi{सब} \hi{ठीक}?} (\emph{sab ṭhīk?}) — \textquotedblleft{}all well?\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}everything fine?\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{सब}} is \textquotedblleft{}all\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\hi{ठीक}} is the \textquotedblleft{}fine\textquotedblright{} you know. The answer: \textbf{\hi{हाँ}, \hi{सब} \hi{ठीक}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A two-word greeting and its answer.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sab ṭhīk?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sab ṭhīk?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{sab ṭhīk?}, then answer \emph{hā̃, sab ṭhīk}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for I have to go, then the Hindi for how's it going, then say \emph{sab ṭhīk?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{सब} \hi{ठीक}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}All well?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bahut din ho gae]{\hi{बहुत} \hi{दिन} \hi{हो} \hi{गए} (bahut din ho gae) — it's been a long time}

\label{lesson:HI-C123-bahutdin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for how's it going, then the Hindi for all well.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{बहुत} \hi{दिन} \hi{हो} \hi{गए}}
\textbf{\hi{बहुत} \hi{दिन} \hi{हो} \hi{गए}} (\emph{bahut din ho gae}) — \textquotedblleft{}it's been a long time\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}many days have become\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{बहुत}} and \textbf{\hi{दिन}} are both yours already.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A greeting for someone you have not seen in a while.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahut din ho gae}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahut din ho gae}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bahut din ho gae!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for how's it going, then the Hindi for all well, then say \emph{bahut din ho gae} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{बहुत} \hi{दिन} \hi{हो} \hi{गए} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}It's been a long time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kyā cal rahā hai?]{\hi{क्या} \hi{चल} \hi{रहा} \hi{है}? (kyā cal rahā hai?) — what's going on?}

\label{lesson:HI-C123-kyachal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for all well, then the Hindi for it's been a long time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{क्या} \hi{चल} \hi{रहा} \hi{है}?}
\textbf{\hi{क्या} \hi{चल} \hi{रहा} \hi{है}?} (\emph{kyā cal rahā hai?}) — \textquotedblleft{}what's going on?\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}what's up?\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\hi{चलना}}, \textquotedblleft{}to go, to move\textquotedblright{}, in the right-now form: what is moving in your life?

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A friendly opener.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kyā cal rahā hai?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kyā cal rahā hai?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{kyā cal rahā hai?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for all well, then the Hindi for it's been a long time, then say \emph{kyā cal rahā hai?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{क्या} \hi{चल} \hi{रहा} \hi{है}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}What's going on?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[khānā khāyā?]{\hi{खाना} \hi{खाया}? (khānā khāyā?) — have you eaten?}

\label{lesson:HI-C123-khanakhaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for it's been a long time, then the Hindi for what's going on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{खाना} \hi{खाया}?}
\textbf{\hi{खाना} \hi{खाया}?} (\emph{khānā khāyā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}have you eaten?\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{खाना}} is both \textquotedblleft{}food\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}to eat\textquotedblright{}: you \emph{ate the eating}. Around a mealtime it is a greeting and a kindness.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
How's it going, all well, long time, what's up, have you eaten.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khānā khāyā?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khānā khāyā?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{khānā khāyā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for it's been a long time, then the Hindi for what's going on, then say \emph{khānā khāyā?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{खाना} \hi{खाया}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Have you eaten?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
